area: ANIMATION (all characters): clip-by-clip critique, rig and pipeline analysis, plan for professional replacements (Blender authoring + Unity runtime layer)
summary:
VERDICT: The animation set is below a shippable bar, and several problems directly cause the user's complaint that you "can't tell when to parry". Six problems matter most:

1. **Damage fires before the visible hit.** Several enemy attacks deal damage before the weapon visibly lands, so the parry window (and the new ground telegraph ring, which is driven by the same StrikeEta) disagrees with what the player sees.
   - Gorō Combo1 is active at 0.58-0.74 s, but the hammer hits at about 0.83 s.
   - Gorō Combo3 is active at 0.39-0.54 s; the hammer hits at about 0.63 s.
   - Gorō's Heavy slam shockwave fires at take-off (1.63 s), about 0.6 s before he lands (2.3 s).
   - Sumo slap1 is active from 0.44 s, but the team's own DealDamage event is at 0.567 s.
2. **Weak tells.**
   - Ninja Attack2 begins already wound up: a 58° pose pop on the 0.08 s crossfade, zero telegraph, contact about 0.3 s later.
   - Most wind-ups are vertical (sword or hammer raised overhead). From the 52° camera that foreshortens to about 62% and overlaps the head.
   - No attack has a designed "tell" hold pose; the code fakes one by slowing the clip to 15%.
3. **Locomotion skates.**
   - Kaito's run is a slow jog: the planted foot moves at 2.3-2.5 m/s while the body moves at 6.2 m/s, so the feet skate 2.5x. The loop also pops 42°.
   - Gorō's legs run too fast: about 7 m/s against a 3.8 m/s body, so he moonwalks.
   - There are no walk, strafe, start, stop or turn clips. Strafing enemies crab-slide on a 40% blend of their forward run.
4. **The hand and foot rig breaks blends.**
   - On Kaito, the sumo, Gorō and the grandpa, the hand and foot deform bones are children of IK target bones parented at the armature root, not of the forearm or shin.
   - Every crossfade therefore detaches wrists and ankles mid-blend. I simulated it: 4-9% of character height, up to 21 cm on the sumo.
   - This topology also makes any bone-level runtime procedural (look-at, spine lean, hit reactions) impossible without the hands floating off.
5. **The core feel clips are placeholders.**
   - ParryStance is 4 frames, then a dead hold.
   - ParrySuccess is a 1-frame blade teleport, then static.
   - Kaito's Hit is the same take as Blocked (curve-for-curve).
   - The dash plays its crouch anticipation while already travelling.
   - Deaths are a whole-model -75° plank rotation over clips that show a character standing.
   - The sumo's 11 m/s "charge" plays a jump/belly-flop in place.
   - The grandpa has no idle or walk: one frozen frame that slides.
6. **Dead idles.** Every idle moves only the arms (8-15°); root, legs and head are static.

FEASIBILITY (proven): I wrote two Blender-only prototypes that author new clips by script on the team rigs and export FBX that binds to the existing Unity models.
- **What the prototypes do:**
  - rebuild two-bone IK on the Target/Pole bones, with automatic pole angles (rest error <0.0006)
  - key poses in armature space with easing, Catmull-Rom arcs and lag/overlap
  - bake to FK and seal loops
  - export with settings that reproduce the team files exactly: same GlobalSettings (Y-up, cm, 30 fps), same Armature Lcl rotation and scale (100), same 62/65 bone paths, no extra leaf bones
  - validate by re-import (rest pose identical, IK gap 0.0001)
- **KaitoRunV2:** a 12-frame (0.40 s) chibi sprint with the planted foot at exactly 5.25 m/s (play at 1.18x for 6.2 m/s, no skating), seam 0.04°, 4.2 cm root bob, pelvis yaw and counter-twisting chest, katana trailing behind.
- **NinjaAttack1V2:** a 1.1 s attack with a lateral wind-up that stays visible from the game camera, a 0.17 s moving hold (glint), a 2-frame strike, contact at frame 16 (n=0.485), a clear punish pose and feet planted (0.2 H/s).

RECOMMENDED PIPELINE (hybrid):
- **(a) Blender:** a scripted authoring library plus a "game skeleton" rig cleanup (hands under forearms, feet under shins, Target/Pole weights merged, spring bones for bandana and cloth, every character facing Blender -Y = Unity +Z so modelYaw is 0 everywhere). About 90 clips authored as pose tables, each with a timing sidecar JSON: contact frame, active window, foot plants, authored ground speed. Automated validators and game-camera contact sheets on every export.
- **(b) Unity:** a runtime layer for what clips can't do well: stride-matched speed warping, foot grounding IK, look-at, spring chains, additive directional hit reactions, lean/bank for enemies, impact squash. Attack windows come from the clip sidecars instead of hand-typed normalized numbers.

NOTE: I could not view the Unity contact sheets in clips/ because of the image request limit in this run. Instead I rendered equivalent side and game-camera sheets for every take from the source FBX files. I verified that the .anim files are the same takes: Attackk1.anim matches kaitoGolpes.fbx Atack1 frame by frame within 0.1°.

issues.title: Enemy damage windows fire before the visible impact (Gorō Combo1/Combo3/Heavy, sumo slap1, sumo charge), so parry timing contradicts the animation
issues.evidence:
Blade/hammer tip speed and height per frame vs EnemyArchetypes.cs activeStart/End (Enemy.TickAttack keeps clip and stepNorm in sync, so normalized times compare directly).
- Gorō Combo1 (EnemyArchetypes.cs:128, 0.48-0.62): the hammer is static and raised until f22 (tip speed 0.1-0.9 units/s), the downswing is f23-27 and the impact is at f26 (n=0.69). Damage lands at f18-23 while the hammer is still up, 0.15-0.25 s early.
- Gorō Combo3 (:130, 0.45-0.62): the hold runs to f15, the downswing is f16-21 and the hammer bottoms at f22-25 (n≈0.73). Active is f13-17.
- Gorō Heavy slam (:131, 0.55-0.62 = f50-56): he takes off at f49-50, apex is f62-63 (root +2.03 units, about 2.2 m in game) and the hammer hits the ground at f69-71 (n=0.77). The shockwave and damage fire at take-off, about 0.5 s before landing.
- Sumo Attack1 (:92, 0.70-0.90 = 0.44 s): the team's own DealDamage event in Characters/Sumo/Attack1.anim is at 0.567 s (n=0.89), so damage is 0.12 s early.
- Sumo Special charge (:95, active 0.35-0.85): the clip is a jump/belly-flop in place (root z 13.9% H, ends crouched), played while Boss.cs:197-208 slides the body at 11 m/s.
- The new CombatTelegraphs ring closes at Enemy.StrikeEta, which is derived from the same activeStart, so ring and hit agree with each other but not with the body.
issues.fix:
Immediate data fix in EnemyArchetypes.cs:
- Gorō Combo1: activeStart/End 0.66/0.78.
- Gorō Combo3: 0.70/0.82.
- Gorō Heavy and slam2: 0.76/0.81.
- Sumo slap1 and Ōzeki slap1: 0.85/0.97.
- Leave Gorō Combo2 (contact n 0.53) and ninja A1/A3 (match the team DealDamage events 0.5 s and 0.4 s) as they are.

Structural fix: every new clip exports a timing sidecar (contact frame, active frames, hold frames). generate_assets.py writes it into NindoContent, and Hit(...) in EnemyArchetypes reads the normalized window from it, so no hand-typed numbers can drift. Give the sumo a real charge loop (see the plan).

issues.title: No readable 'tell' poses; ninja Attack2 has zero anticipation; vertical wind-ups foreshortened at the 52° camera
issues.evidence:
Ninja Attack 1 → Attack 2 chain: end/start pose difference 58° on Target_Brazo.L/Mano.L. The 0.08 s crossfade (Enemy.BeginStep, anim.Play(a.state, 0.08f)) teleports the blade from low-front to high-behind through the body. Attack2 starts already wound up, contact is at n=0.47 (≈0.3 s) and it has telegraph 0 (EnemyArchetypes.cs:54), while the parry window is 0.24 s total (perfect 0.11 s, PlayerConfig.cs:51-52).

Wind-ups are vertical:
- Ninja A1 raises the sword straight up at f8-12.
- Gorō Combo1/2/3 hold the hammer overhead.
- At pitch 52° vertical extent projects at cos52 = 0.62 and overlaps the head. The 1.7 m ninja is about 140 px tall at 1080p (24 m, FOV 30), so the blade itself is only a few pixels wide.

No clip contains a designed hold pose. Enemy.TickAttack:449-452 fakes one by playing the clip at 15% speed from activeStart-0.12, so the freeze lands on whatever frame happens to be there (for ninja A1, mid-swing f12-15).

My prototype NinjaAttack1V2 (lateral, silhouette-breaking wind-up plus a 0.17 s moving hold) reads clearly from the target's viewpoint: sheets/proto_ninja_attack_sheet.png, row 1.
issues.fix:
Author every enemy attack with this 'tell' grammar:
1. Wind-up 0.25-0.35 s into a unique, silhouette-breaking tell pose. Keep the weapon outside the body outline as seen from above: lateral or low-behind, with the body coiled 30-50° and sunk 5-8% H.
2. Moving hold of 0.12-0.25 s (1-2° drift plus tremble). The glint VFX fires on the hold's first frame.
3. Strike in 2-3 frames, including a smear frame; the contact frame is activeStart.
4. Follow-through with 10-20% overshoot, then a clear 0.3-0.5 s punish pose.
5. Recovery.

Chained steps start from the previous step's end pose and include their own shorter tell (0.12-0.18 s). Unblockables use a separate tell family that is longer (0.4-0.6 s) and two-handed or crouched.

Remove the 15% slowdown hack once clips carry their own hold; keep AttackDef.telegraph only as an optional extension of the authored hold (difficulty knob).

Tell ladder: ninja 0.45 s from wind-up start to contact, elite 0.35 s, sumo 0.7 s, Gorō 0.8-1.0 s, bosses mixed with feints.

issues.title: Kaito run: 2.5x foot skating, 42° loop pop, bouncy jog instead of sprint; no walk/start/stop/turn
issues.evidence:
AuraRun.anim (= kaitoGolpes RUN, 60 f containing 3 strides of 20 f):
- The planted foot moves backward at 2.33-2.48 m/s at game scale (1.5 m) while PlayerConfig.runSpeed is 6.2 m/s, a 2.5x skate (locomotion_check.py).
- Loop seam is 42.1° on Brazo.L: the arm pops every 1.97 s.
- Root bob is 12.4% of height (bouncy jog).

The blend tree is Idle↔Run on a normalized Speed, so low stick values play a half-weight run while sliding. Idle(f1)→Run blend detaches the ankle 0.109 units (3.9% H) at 50% weight (blend_gap.py). Kaito's legs are about 0.32 m long, so a believable 6.2 m/s needs about 10 steps/s (0.2 s per step).
issues.fix:
Replace with the authored set at 30 fps:
- Walk: 0.8 s / 24 f, authored 1.6 m/s.
- Jog: 0.53 s / 16 f, 3.5 m/s.
- Run: 0.40 s / 12 f, 5.25 m/s. The prototype proto/KaitoRunV2.fbx is ready to polish: planted foot exactly 5.25 m/s, seam 0.04°.
- RunStart: 0.2 s. RunStop: 0.33 s skid with katana overswing. Pivot180: 0.27 s.

Controller changes:
- Locomotion 1D blend thresholds in m/s (0, 1.6, 3.5, 5.25), with the Speed parameter as real velocity.
- Stride warping: Animator speed = actual / authored speed, clamped 0.8-1.25.

Optional: lower runSpeed to about 5.5 for readability.

issues.title: Rig topology (hands/feet parented to IK target bones) detaches wrists/ankles on every crossfade and blocks bone-level procedural animation
issues.evidence:
In kaitooo.fbx the hierarchy is Armature/Targetbrazo.R/Mando.R/KatanaBone and Armature/Targetpie.L/Pie.L: the hands and feet are not under Antebrazo/Tibia. The sumo (TargetBrazo/Palma, TargetPie/pie), Gorō (TargetBrazo/Mano, TargetPie/Pie) and the grandpa (AntebrazoTarget/Mano, TibiaTarget/Pie) have the same topology.

The IK was baked, so each clip on its own is consistent (gap 0.000). Unity blends each transform independently, though. Simulated 50% crossfades:
- Kaito Dash→Run: 0.124 units (4.4% H, about 7 cm).
- Kaito ParrySuccess→Idle: 0.108.
- Gorō Combo3→Idle: 0.106.
- Sumo SpecialAtack→Idle: 0.418 units (8.6% H, about 21 cm).

Any runtime rotation of tronco/cabeza/Antebrazo (look-at, lean, hit react) would leave the hands and katana behind. The ninja rig is clean FK (Mano under Antebrazo, Pie under Tibia), with IK targets parented to Root and not skinned.
issues.fix:
Build a game skeleton per character in Blender (Tools/Blender/anim/game_skeleton.py):
- Reparent Mando/Palma/Mano → Antebrazo and Pie/pie → Tibia.
- Merge the Target*/Pole* vertex groups into the nearest deform bone, then remove all Target/Pole bones from the export.
- Keep the bone names.

Export {char}_model.fbx (mesh + skeleton) and {char}_anims.fbx (armature only, all takes). In Blender the team animates on a control rig whose deform skeleton copies its transforms; export bakes them. Retarget the existing team clips onto the game skeleton by baking with Copy Transforms, so the game keeps working during the transition.

Until then, keep crossfades between unmatched poses at or below 0.06 s.

issues.title: Parry clips (the core feel of the game) are placeholders
issues.evidence:
ParryStance = TrueBlock.anim: 0.10 s / 4 f. It snaps to guard in 3 frames, then holds a dead pose for the rest of the 0.24 s window plus 0.28 s recover. Pie.L slides at 2.1 H/s within those 4 frames.

ParrySuccess = Parried.anim (Blender 'Parry', 0.233 s / 8 f):
- The blade teleports between f3 and f4 (tip 42 H/s, bearing -42°→-123° in one frame), then everything is static from f5 to f8.
- Pie.L slides at 3.4 H/s.
- The end pose is 118° away from Idle (Targetbrazo.R), so the blend detaches the wrist by 0.108 units.

There is no deflection impact frame, recoil or counter-ready pose. The design doc says the parry should 'light up the scene'.
issues.fix:
Author these clips:
- ParryStance: 0.10 s / 3 f into the guard pose.
- ParryHold: 0.5 s loop with tremble and a breathing chest.
- ParrySuccess_L and ParrySuccess_R: 0.30 s / 9 f. Blade snaps across the incoming line, impact pose holds 2 f (pairs with hit-stop), recoil 1 step, ends in a counter-ready pose matched to Attack1's start, so the riposte chains with zero blend.
- PerfectParry: 0.40 s flourish with the spark pose.
- Blocked: 0.40 s recoil when Kaito's own attack is guarded.

Pick L or R from the attacker's side (dot product of Kaito.right and the direction to the attacker).

issues.title: Hit reactions and deaths: Kaito's Hit is the Blocked clip; enemy deaths are rigid model rotations over standing clips
issues.evidence:
Kaito's Hit uses 'Preiliminar Kaito/Stunned.anim', which is curve-for-curve identical to Blockk.anim (identical per-bone key counts and ranges for all 20 major bones). Being hit therefore looks the same as having your attack blocked (generate_assets.py:561). The unused 'hitt' (8 f) and 'NotBlock' (10 f) takes exist in kaitoGolpes.fbx.

Enemy deaths:
- Ninja death = Stuned.anim (2.63 s): knocked back, then stands up into an idle-like stance.
- Sumo death = Cansado (looping tired idle).
- Gorō death = StunSpin (dizzy loop).
- Meanwhile Enemy.DeathRoutine (Enemy.cs:740-749) rotates the whole model -75° as a plank and slides it 0.8 m. The player gets the same treatment (PlayerController.cs:497-508, -80°).

Ninja Hit = Damaged (0.23 s): a tiny head nod with a 2.3 H/s foot slide.
issues.fix:
Hit reactions: author Hit_Light front and back (0.30 s / 9 f) and Hit_Heavy / knockback (0.7 s) per character. Add a procedural directional additive (spring on spine/head away from the hit direction, about 0.25 s) so 2 clips cover all directions.

Deaths per character: Kaito 1.2 s, ninja 1.0 s collapse to knees then forward, sumo 1.4 s topples like a tree, Gorō 2.0 s to knees with the hammer dropped. Also an Executed victim clip (1.0 s) synced to the finisher contact. Remove the plank rotation when a death clip exists, and keep the smoke dissolve.

issues.title: Sumo action/clip mismatches: charge plays a jump, stomp plays a push
issues.evidence:
Special (charge, 11 m/s, Boss.cs:197-208) uses SpecialAttack.anim, which is a standing arms-up jump ending in a belly-flop crouch (0.77 s, root z 13.9% H). The sumo skates about 4 m during active n 0.35-0.85, and the 0.45 s telegraph shows him just standing.

Attack3 'stomp' (360° shockwave, EnemyArchetypes.cs:94) uses Attack3.anim: arms crossed and static for f16-32, then a forward shove at f35. The feet never lift (pie.L z range 1% H), so a ground-pound mechanic plays a push animation.

Sumo Hit = Blocked.anim is a good stumble but lasts 1.63 s.

Also, Enemy.TickSpecial (Enemy.cs:507) does not move non-boss sumos during 'charge'; only Boss.cs implements it.
issues.fix:
Author these sumo clips:
- ChargeTell: 0.5 s. Shikiri crouch with fists to the ground, head-down stare; this is the unblockable tell.
- ChargeLoop: 0.6 s tachiai run, authored at 9 m/s, head-down sprint.
- ChargeEnd and WallHit: 0.6 s.
- Stomp: 1.4 s shiko. Leg raised high and held 0.25 s, contact at 0.9 s, then belly jiggle.
- Slap1 and Slap2 (tsuppari): 0.9 s, with the arm cocked laterally as the tell.
- Hit: 0.4 s, belly jiggle.
- Parried: reuse the Blocked stumble, trimmed to 1.0 s.

Check that common sumos are spawned as a class that implements charge.

issues.title: Enemy locomotion: crab-skating strafe, Gorō moonwalk, sumo skate
issues.evidence:
Enemy.TickStrafe (Enemy.cs:339-351) circles the target at walkSpeed while facing it. The only locomotion is a 1D Idle↔Run blend on v/runSpeed (generate_assets.py controller()), so a strafing ninja at 2 m/s plays 60% idle + 40% forward run while moving sideways.

Stance-foot speed vs body speed:
- Ninja run: 3.7-4.0 vs 5.0 m/s (1.3x skate).
- Sumo walk used as run: 2.4 vs 3.4 m/s (1.4x).
- Gorō Run: 6.8-7.0 vs 3.8 m/s (0.55x, legs moonwalk).
issues.fix:
Author Walk, Run, StrafeL, StrafeR and Backstep for the ninja and sumo, and Walk/Run for Gorō, all with authored speeds in the sidecar.
- Controller: a 2D freeform-directional blend tree (local velocity X/Z) for enemies, plus stride warping (Animator speed = actual/authored speed, clamp 0.7-1.4).
- Stopgap: set m_TimeScale on the run child of the Gorō blend tree to 0.55 and on Kaito AuraRun to 2.0.

issues.title: Loop seams pop
issues.evidence:
First vs last key, per bone:
- Kaito AuraRun.anim: 42.1° (Brazo.L), loopTime 1.
- Ninja Exausto.anim: 25.6° (Antebrazo.L), loopTime 1.
- Gorō StunSpin: 133° (Blender take StunSpinn, loopTime True in MINIJEFE_CLIPS).
- Kaito Dash.anim (loopTime 1): 101.5°, harmless only because it is cut short.
issues.fix: The authoring library seals every loop by copying the first key to the last and keys the cycle as periodic functions or closed Catmull-Rom (prototype seam 0.04°). The validator fails any loop above 1°.

issues.title: Dash and Finisher timing/holds
issues.evidence:
Dash: Dash.anim (0.77 s) plays at 1.4x for dashDuration 0.26 s + recover 0.08 s (PlayerController.Combat.cs:310). The first 6 frames are a crouch anticipation, played while the code already moves Kaito 6.5 m. Frames 7-15 are a static hold (tip speed 0). The end pose is 117° from Run, so blending into Run detaches the ankle by 0.124 units.

Finisher: Finishing.anim (2.67 s @1.7x) holds a completely static pose for f35-57 (0.45 s real time) and slashes in 2 frames (f58-60). The strike timing itself matches the team event Fbx1 at 1.867 s and the code's n=0.68.
issues.fix:
Dash: 0.26 s / 8 f. Starts already in the low streamlined pose (at most 1 anticipation frame, before the code moves), katana and bandana trailing, brake on f7-8. DashRecover: 0.10 s, pose-matched to Run f0.

Finisher: 1.3 s. Iaido draw tension as a moving hold (breathing, tremble, bandana lift), vanish frame at contact (sidecar event), chiburi blade flick, 0.4 s sheathe.

issues.title: Lifeless idles; grandpa has no idle or walk
issues.evidence:
Only the arms move in every idle; root and legs are static:
- Kaito Idle: forearm 14°, tronco 4.5°, head 0.5°, root bob 0.1% H.
- Ninja Idle: 9.5°.
- Sumo Idle: 14.6°.
- Gorō Idle: nearly static.

Grandpa: Idle = 2-frame slice (0.033 s) of the kidnap take (generate_assets.py:599). Locomotion uses Idle for both idle and run, so NPC.SlideTo (StoryDirector.cs:149, :346) slides a frozen statue.
issues.fix:
Idles with weight shift (pelvis 1-2 cm side-to-side), breathing in chest and shoulders (2-3°), head micro look-arounds, and katana grip adjustments; 2.0-3.0 s loops plus one fidget variant each.

Combat idle vs. exploration idle for Kaito and the ninja.

Grandpa: Idle (2.5 s, hunched breathing), Walk (1.0 s at 0.9 m/s), 2 talk-gesture loops, Bow, Hug (ending).

issues.title: Rig hygiene: control bones skin vertices, duplicate skeletons/files, inconsistent forward axes
issues.evidence:
Vertex groups with weight >0.01:
- Kaito: Polebrazo.R 7 verts, Targetpie.L/R 84/86, Targetbrazo.L/R 43.
- Sumo: PolePie.L/R 16 each, TargetPie/TargetBrazo 62 each.

Pole bones float in front of the knees and elbows, so those vertices drag whenever a pole moves.

Grandpa.fbx has 82 bones: a duplicated '.001' skeleton (the grandpa mesh is skinned to the .001 set, the kidnap ninja to the other).

There are 6 Kaito FBX copies with identical rigs (kaitooo, kaito, kaitoGolpes, 'kaito dadadadad', FinisherKaito, Models/kaito_.fbx, UIOAWUH....fbx).

Forward axes differ per file: Kaito and ninja face Blender +X, the sumo +Y, Gorō -Y, the grandpa +Y with axis_forward '-Z'. That is why CharacterEntry.modelYaw needs 90/180/0/180.
issues.fix:
game_skeleton.py:
- Normalize every character to face Blender -Y (= Unity +Z with axis_forward='-Z', axis_up='Y'), so modelYaw is 0 for all.
- Merge control-bone weights into deform bones.
- Split the grandpa and the kidnap ninja into separate armatures.

Keep one source FBX per character and move the duplicates to _Legacy.

Add a validator in Blender at export and an EditMode test in Unity. It samples each character's locomotion clip and asserts that the planted foot travels along -Z in model space, that the nose and katana are on +Z within 10°, and that the feet rest at y=0 ±2 cm.

issues.title: Kaito attack spacing: heavy finisher slower than lights; feet slide during attacks
issues.evidence:
Peak tip speed:
- Attack1: 15.7 H/s at f7.
- Attack2: 15.4 H/s.
- Attack3 (the heavy combo ender): only 9.4 H/s, with no impact hold. hitStop 0.11 compensates.

Attack1 over-rotates tronco by 130° and turns the head 89° away from the target. Planted-foot slide: Attack1 Pie.L 1.75 H/s, Attack2 Pie.R 2.73 H/s, ParrySuccess 3.43 H/s.

The Attack1→2→3 chain is pose-continuous (0.5°), which is good.
issues.fix:
Re-author the combo:
- Attack1: 0.40 s / 12 f. Anticipation 4 f, contact f5-6, follow-through 3 f.
- Attack2: 0.37 s / 11 f, the mirrored return diagonal.
- Attack3: 0.60 s / 18 f. 6 f wind-up, jump-lunge or spin, 3 f impact hold, wider arc.

The head keeps looking at the target (runtime look-at), feet are planted or stepping with IK-locked contacts, and each end pose matches the next start pose and the Run/Idle entry.

issues.title: Useful team takes unused
issues.evidence:
These takes are never referenced by generate_assets.py controllers():
- kaitoGolpes.fbx: hitt (8 f), NotBlock (10 f).
- Ninjadesequilibrio.fbx: Desequilibrio (75 f).
- Sumo 2.fbx: desequilibrio (80 f), Atack1.001 (10 f).
- nindo).fbx: a different Block (89 f) and Parry (15 f).
issues.fix: Use them as references or blocking for the new clips (e.g. hitt for Kaito Hit_Light, desequilibrio for the Exhausted poses), then archive them.

plan:
GOAL: low-poly stylized characters, very detailed and believable motion, a readable parry game. Hybrid pipeline: authored clips in Blender (scripted pose tables plus team hand-keys) on cleaned game skeletons, plus a thin Unity runtime layer.

PHASE 0 — stopgap data fixes (no new art; lead, about 1 h)
1. EnemyArchetypes.cs:
   - Gorō Combo1: activeStart/End 0.66/0.78. Combo3: 0.70/0.82. Heavy and slam2: 0.76/0.81.
   - Sumo slap1 and Ōzeki slap1: 0.85/0.97.
   - Ninja Attack2: add telegraph 0.15 and use Play fade 0.15 for chained steps.
2. generate_assets.py controller(): m_TimeScale on the run child of the Gorō blend tree = 0.55, and on Kaito AuraRun = 2.0, to cut skating until the new runs land.

PHASE 1 — Blender authoring framework (new Tools/Blender/anim/, generalized from my prototypes)
- nindo_anim.py:
  - load_rig(char)
  - add_ik(bone, target, pole): auto pole angle by minimizing rest error; measured -177.2/90.1/-2.8/89.9° on Kaito and -95/-0.8/-85/180 on the ninja.
  - set_ctrl(name, pos, rot): armature-space and parent-aware via PoseBone.matrix. Required on the ninja, whose IK targets are children of Root; otherwise the feet slide with the hips (measured 0.80 → 0.21 H/s after the fix).
  - Pose tables per frame with per-segment easing (inout/in/out/snap/lin), Catmull-Rom arcs for root, hands and feet, slerped weapon direction (the blade axis is measured from the weapon mesh in hand space), lagged sampling for overlap (head 1 f, off-hand 2 f, chest 0.08 cycle), moving holds (tremble 0.5-1 cm), reach clamp at 97% of limb length.
  - bake(): nla.bake visual_keying, clear_constraints, then seal loops.
  - export(): axis_forward='-Z', axis_up='Y', apply_unit_scale=True, apply_scale_options='FBX_SCALE_NONE', add_leaf_bones=False, primary 'Y', secondary 'X', bake_anim_use_all_actions=True, simplify 0, step 1. Verified to reproduce the team files' GlobalSettings (Y-up, cm, TimeMode 30 fps), the Armature Lcl rotation (-90,-90,0) and scale (100), and identical bone paths, so clips bind to the existing Unity models.
